Picture 3 shows from left to right: the boy Ben, the girl Nan, the grown woman Teacher Kim, and a puppy (the puppy must NOT appear in this picture). Picture 4 shows a green classroom door. Picture 5 shows a wall of big colorful animal pictures. Picture 6 shows a red school bag with a yellow label and blue straps. Copy each person exactly as shown. The picture: a wide, bright kindergarten classroom shot, the camera at a low height, in the room of picture 1. At the back, the green door of picture 4 is closed in the wall at the right, and the animal pictures of picture 5 hang on the wall at the left. The six children stand in a row in the front, large, full-body, all facing the camera and all waving hello with one raised open hand and a big happy smile. Their order from the left: Ben, Mia, Sam, May, Pat, Nan. Pat has the red school bag on his back with one small round bump on the flap, as if something moves inside; he shows his side a little so that the bag is seen. Teacher Kim stands behind the children, in the middle, smaller because she is farther away, and smiles. Exactly seven people and no dog. A hand that reaches toward the camera looks larger because of perspective; that is correct. Clean eye corners with no skin flaps, no streak on the forehead, and no marks on the face. Rendering errors to NOT copy from the character pictures: a tiny dark tick mark or pale skin flap at the outer corner of an eye (the corner next to the ear), and a faint pale crease on a forehead. Each eye ends in a smooth, rounded corner. Nan alone keeps one short, thick, curved eyelash flick at each outer eye corner. The page text is "Hello!" and is context only: do not draw any text. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no writing on any picture or sign. The picture is for young children and is rated G. Important: the school bag on Pat's back is CLOSED. One clearly round, soft, dome-shaped bump, about the size of a small puppy's head, pushes up the flap on the top of the bag, as if something moves inside. The bump is a smooth round dome of the same red cloth; nothing sticks out of the bag, and the bag has no open pocket. Every hand and every foot is fully inside the picture: leave a clear margin at the left and right edges, so the six children stand a little closer together and a little smaller. Pat stands turned away from the others: his back is three quarters toward the camera, so that the red school bag on his back, with its one round dome-shaped bump, shows large and clear, and he looks back over his shoulder at the camera and waves. The other five children face the camera.

Every person keeps a face with two eyes with pupils and a mouth. Draw each head of hair as one closed shape. Simplify the background: draw only a few large, simple, closed shapes. No small details, no grass blades, no small leaves, no hatching, no tick marks, no wood grain lines. Every shape is closed with one thick line.
